blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The recommendations of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) are purely advisory in nature and not binding on the government.
The NHRC has no power to punish human rights violators or directly award monetary relief or compensation to victims.
The Commission cannot inquire into any matter after the expiry of one year from the date on which the human rights violation was committed.
Powers of the NHRC regarding human rights violations committed by members of the armed forces are severely restricted.

rows: Recommendations are purely advisory and non-binding on authorities
Inquires into complaints of human rights abuse
Cannot investigate cases filed after 1 year of the incident
Cannot conduct independent direct investigations into armed forces

items: Statute of Limitation: NHRC is barred from inquiring into any case after 1 year from the date of occurrence.
Non-binding Decisions: NHRC lacks judicial authority to enforce its orders or punish offenders directly.
Armed Forces Jurisdiction: NHRC can only seek a report from the Central Government regarding human rights violations by armed forces.
